newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa takes a tumble after NY rally falters.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa takes a tumble after NY rally falters.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures reversed direction and ended Tuesday broadly lower on profit-taking after a fall in New York, traders said.
New York's September contract hit a new eight-year-peak of $1,655 per tonne but slipped back after failing to break the major trendline which goes as far back as December.
"This sparked profit-taking. Sell-stops were hit and London was knocked down as well," one trader said.
London's September, which was in the plus column throughout the morning, and changed course to end the day 11 stg lower at 1,112 stg per tonne. Its intraday low was 1,097.
July was also 18 stg down at 1,088 stg.
The market was earlier supported by trade buying on July and an absence of origin offers.
But major manufacturers were also sidelined, deterred by the firmer sterling against major European units.
Building on the hefty gains recorded late last week, the September contract hit a new one-year high of 1,140 stg on Monday although it closed the day off with pared gains.
The rally was fuelled by talk of a preliminary forecast for a smaller 1997/98 Ivorian crop and a developing weather pattern called El Nino.
Just before the upward move, prices had been kept at below 1,020 stg level.
Traders said the market could now try to consolidate or correct slightly lower in a correction to an overbought situation before assuming another direction.
"But consolidation could mean prices rising by 30 stg or falling by 40 stg," one trader said.
Futures volume reached 8,738 lots. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
